text:
Incident Bot: P1: elevated 5xx + tail latency observed on monolith-capital-vpc (dedicated pool) at 2026-03-18T14:03:00Z
Aisha Khan: acked. Paging in. seeing sharp p95 spike at 14:02 UTC, errors concentrated on pool 'monolith-vpc-prod'
Ben Park: checking kube events and OOMs now
Ben Park: node-12 has several OOM_kill entries and kubelet restart churn, looks noisy
Marco Ruiz: could be cache retention + long-context jobs. Monolith does lots of >8k token seqs this morning per telemetry
Aisha Khan: sitting on metrics dashboard — kv-cache miss rate doubled starting 14:01, memory RSS climbing on a few runtimes
Leah Torres - CS: pinging Monolith contact (Samir) to say we saw failures and are investigating. Will keep them in loop.
Incident Bot: auto-runbook: start noisy-tenant isolation? (yes/no)
Aisha Khan: yes. Plan: isolate Monolith tenant to a frozen subset, drain other tenants off noisy nodes, scale pool +1 replica from reserve, and enable per-tenant token limit for 30m.
Ben Park: executing drain on node-12 and cordon
```
# cordon node
rctl nodes cordon node-12 --reason "oom-noise"
# drain
rctl nodes drain node-12 --timeout 300s
# scale pool
rctl pool update monolith-vpc-prod --replicas 7
```
Aisha Khan: started a temporary per-tenant token cap for Monolith to 12k tokens to blunt runaway sequences
DevOps Bot: action taken: node-12 cordoned; pool scaled to 7 replicas at 2026-03-18T14:08:21Z
Marco Ruiz: after isolation, 5xx dropped from ~5.8% to 1.1% within 6m. Tail latency p99 improved but p95 still a bit high (360ms)
Leah Torres - CS: Monolith SRE (via DM): they saw the same beginning at 14:00 and confirm they pushed some large-batch analytics queries around 13:58. They appreciate isolate/scale action.
Aisha Khan: taking heap snapshots and kv-cache diagnostics from affected workers. Tagging eng-ml for memory leak hypothesis.
Marco Ruiz: grabbing heap dump from worker-14 and kv-cache histogram. early look: retention spikes in rdx.kv_store when sequence length >10k — some entries not expiring as expected
Ben Park: no new OOMs after cordon/drain. system load normalizing.
Incident Bot: incident 3112345678 severity reduced to MONITORING at 2026-03-18T14:32:05Z
Aisha Khan: preparing handoff to Ryan for night watch — will keep per-tenant cap and isolation for 8h, then carefully relax if stable
Ryan (oncall): taking over. escalation criteria: error rate >2% sustained for 10m or new OOM on any worker. I'll check at 15:30, 17:30, 20:00 UTC.
Leah Torres - CS: drafting customer update to Monolith execs. proposed language: "We detected transient resource pressure affecting your dedicated pool starting ~14:00 UTC, isolated your traffic to reduce cross-tenant impact, and scaled capacity to restore service. No customer data was lost. We're performing a root-cause investigation and will follow up with a technical report and remediation timeline."
Legal Ops: please review draft before send. Also advise on SLA-credit phrasing if requested.
Leah Torres - CS: sent DM to Monolith SRE with brief message; they requested an exec-level call tomorrow 09:00 PT.
Marco Ruiz: quick dev note: instrumenting kv_store eviction logs and adding a defensive eviction pass to reject items older than 24h. will try a small staging patch then canary to one node.
Aisha Khan: attaching metric snapshots and log snippets to incident doc.
Ben Park: logs snippet:
```
Mar 18 14:01:59 worker-14 redwood-runtime: rdx.kv_store: retain_count=105432, evict_misses=12
Mar 18 14:02:03 worker-14 kernel: Out of memory: Kill process 22345 (python) score 785
```
Leah Torres - CS: Monolith asks if this qualifies for SLA credit. They lost ~28 minutes of success-rate degradation during peak. Suggest we propose a standard credit + tech debrief.
Legal Ops: standard approach: offer proportional credit per reserved-capacity SLA and include a technical debrief + exec briefing. We'll draft a non-admission statement and sign-off language.
Aisha Khan: incident doc action items (flat list):
- collect heap dumps & KV metrics (owner: Marco)
- patch and test defensive eviction (owner: Marco)
- add tenant noisy-throttle automation (owner: Ben)
- customer comms & credit proposal (owner: Leah)
- postmortem writeup (owner: Aisha)
All due within 72h except patch which target 2026-03-21 for canary
Marco Ruiz: will open a PR with TTL enforcement and more aggressive background eviction. Regression tests added for long-sequence workloads.
Leah Torres - CS: sent initial customer-facing note (subject: Service disruption on monolith-capital-vpc) at 14:45 UTC. Monolith acknowledged and asked for RCA by EOD tomorrow and exec call at 16:00 UTC.
Nimbus SRE: thanks for quick action. Confirmed they saw errors spike when their analytics job kicked off; they will modify scheduling to stagger heavy jobs for now.
Legal Ops: reviewed draft credit wording; Leah, please don't promise specific dollar amounts in thread. We'll route a formal credit estimate via Finance after mapping to SLA formula.
Aisha Khan: RI: long-term mitigation: automated tenant isolation when a tenant's per-minute token consumption exceeds X for Y minutes. Priya's quota system could surface this as a trigger.
Ben Park: started a run of canary test for patch on staging.
Ryan (oncall): 20:05 UTC check-in: all stable, no regressions. Keeping monitoring for 12h then close. I'll mark as resolved when we've had 12h continuous stability.
Leah Torres - CS: customer exec call scheduled and accepted for 2026-03-19 16:00 UTC. Drafting slide deck: timeline, mitigation, next steps, credit approach.
Marco Ruiz: :thumbsup: PR open. small behavior change but adds safety net for retention bugs. Planning canary deploy next maintenance window.
Leah Torres - CS: post-incident follow-ups: send customer-friendly RCA after Legal approves wording, include offer for reserved-capacity credit and 1:1 technical debrief.
Legal Ops: will provide approved template by EOD.
Aisha Khan: closing live mitigation; moving incident to POSTMORTEM state and assigning writeup. Thanks team.
Incident Bot: incident 3112345678 state changed to POSTMORTEM at 2026-03-18T20:10:00Z
